cards.text: Jeremiah, God’s prophet, has a word for the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and he skips the small talk. He opens with “Listen and give heed. Do not be arrogant…” Then he tells them WHY.

cards.question: Why does Jeremiah tell the people of Judah not to be arrogant?

answers.text: Because the king has commanded it

cards.text: Next he says, “Give glory to the LORD your God before He brings darkness, before your feet stumble on the dusky mountains.” Friend, that’s hiking down a mountain at sunset when your phone flashlight dies at 1 percent.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the people wait for light, but the LORD turns it into deep gloom and thick darkness.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah tells them what he’ll do if they don’t listen. And this is where you see the prophet’s heart.

cards.question: If the people of Judah don’t listen, what will Jeremiah do?

answers.text: Weep in secret because of their pride
Leave Jerusalem and never come back
Stop bringing them the LORD’s word

cards.question: Jeremiah says his eyes will overflow with tears. What has happened that makes him cry?

answers.text: The LORD’s flock has been taken captive
The temple has been torn to the ground
The king has turned the city against him

cards.text: Now a message goes ALL the way to the top: to the king and to the queen mother.

cards.question: The message to the king and the queen mother: “Take a ___ seat, for your glorious crowns have fallen from your heads.”

cards.text: From glorious crowns to a lowly seat, that’s first class to the seat by the restroom, and there is NO upgrade coming. And it’s not just the palace: the cities of the Negev have been shut tight, and no one can open them.

cards.question: Jeremiah says only a few towns of Judah have been carried into exile.

cards.text: Jeremiah’s message keeps going, and now it’s a call to look up. Lift up your eyes, it says, and see who’s coming.

cards.question: The message says to lift up your eyes and see who’s coming. From which direction are they coming?

cards.text: Then comes a hard question: “Where is the flock entrusted to you, the sheep that were your pride?” That’s the dog sitter when the owner walks in, looks around and says, “So… where’s Max?”
And then: “What will you say when He sets over you close allies whom you yourself trained?” That’s training the new guy at work, and a month later he’s your BOSS.

cards.question: When those allies are set over them, pangs of anguish grip them, as they do a woman in ___.

cards.text: Then the message sees the next question coming: “Why has this happened to me?” And it answers it straight.

cards.question: The answer to “Why has this happened to me?” is that their enemies were simply too strong for them.

cards.text: It’s the magnitude of their iniquity, and the picture is public shame: skirts stripped off, the body exposed. Then comes the line this passage is famous for: “Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?”

cards.question: “Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?” What is that question saying about the people?

answers.text: They can’t do good when they’re used to evil
They will change once the trouble comes
They are no worse than the other nations

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks: “I will scatter you like chaff driven by the desert wind.”

cards.question: The LORD says this is their lot, the portion He has measured to them, because they have ___ Him and trusted in ___.

cards.text: So He will pull their skirts up over their face, so their shame may be seen. And He names it: adulteries, lustful neighings, shameless prostitution on the hills and in the fields.

cards.question: The LORD says Jerusalem’s detestable acts have stayed hidden from Him.
The LORD ends with “Woe to you, O Jerusalem!” and then a question. What does He ask?

answers.text: How long will you remain unclean
Why did you turn back to Egypt
Who will rebuild your fallen walls

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "Take a ___ seat, for your glorious crowns have fallen from your heads.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This is a why question: it asks why the LORD measures out this portion. Only two of the five words fit blank 1, "forgotten" and "obeyed". "Chariots" and "silver" fit only blank 2. "Obeyed" is not a believable reason for being scattered like chaff, so blank 1 gives itself away. Replace "obeyed" with a believable wrong verb, such as "feared" or "served". Make sure the replacement is false everywhere in the passage and is not close in meaning to "forgotten".

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The card is only "Then the LORD speaks:" followed by the verse 24 quote. It has none of Papa Dorin's voice and nothing that carries the moment, such as a reaction or a storyteller's line.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
